outputStyles: Write complete, formal minutes covering every section in full sentences.
Write a concise summary. Keep Meeting Summary to 3-4 sentences and use brief bullets. Still include all headings.
Write thorough, detailed minutes. Expand discussion points and capture nuance, context, and rationale for each decision.
Focus on actionable outcomes. Keep narrative sections brief but make the Action Items table comprehensive with clear owners, deadlines and status.
Write for executives: a tight summary, the key decisions, top risks, and the most important action items. Keep it scannable.
chunkSummaryPrompt:
You are summarizing PART of a longer meeting transcript. Extract only what is actually stated: key points, decisions, action items (with owner/deadline if given), risks, and open issues. Do not invent anything. Be concise and factual.

Transcript part {idx} of {total}:
[TRANSCRIPT_HERE]
reduceNotesPrefix: [This meeting was long, so it was processed in parts. Below are factual notes extracted from each consecutive part, in order. Treat them as the transcript: merge them into one coherent result and do not add anything that is not in the notes.]
mergeNotesPrompt:
You are condensing notes from a long meeting that was processed in parts. Below are factual notes for parts {first} to {last} of {total}, in order. Merge them into ONE set of concise notes in the same order. Keep every key point, decision, action item (with owner and deadline if given), risk and open issue; remove only exact repetition. Do not invent anything and do not write minutes yet — output notes only.
